# Helix Design System — LLM Index

> Helix DS · v0.1.0 · Native HTML elements + hand-written WAI-ARIA, Tailwind CSS v4, Tabler Icons,
> DTCG tokens. React 19 + TypeScript strict. Every component has a machine-readable contract.

## Quick reference

- Scope: @helix-ds · Token prefix: --helix- · Data attribute prefix: data-helix-
- Prop vocabulary (canonical names + anti-synonyms): .ai/maps/prop-map.md
- Rules for agents building with Helix: AGENTS.md

## Packages

- @helix-ds/core    — every component, plus globals.css (import '@helix-ds/core/globals.css')
- @helix-ds/tokens  — tokens as CSS custom properties (import '@helix-ds/tokens/helix.css') + TS constants
- Icons: @tabler/icons-react, always rendered through core's Icon component or a component's icon prop

## Components

All import from '@helix-ds/core'. Status (draft/beta/stable) is computed — contracts/stability.json
(ADR-018). Full spec per component: contracts/components/{Name}.json. This list is generated from
contracts/manifest.json on every commit.

<!-- helix:component-list:start -->
- Accordion (core) — A single collapsible disclosure — a header that expands/collapses a panel of content, with no JS height measurement needed.
- AppShell (layout) — The top-level page shell — composes a SideNav, a TopBar, and the scrollable main content into one consistent full-height layout.
- Avatar (core) — Represents a person or entity as a small circular image or initials indicator — a table row, a nav footer, a comment author.
- AvatarGroup (core) — Shows several people or entities associated with the same record as a compact overlapping stack of Avatars, collapsing whatever doesn't fit into a '+N' count.
- Badge (core) — Communicates status, category labels, or counts in a compact, high-contrast capsule.
- Button (core) — Triggers an action or navigates to a destination when pressed by the user.
- Card (core) — Groups related content in a visually distinct, flat surface — a dashboard widget, a settings group, a gallery tile.
- Chart (core) — Visualizes a metric with a token-branded, accessible chart so people can understand trends, comparisons, composition, or events.
- Checkbox (core) — Lets users select one or more independent options from a set, or confirm a single binary choice.
- CheckboxGroup (core) — Lets users choose zero or more options from a small, visible set of independent choices.
- Chip (core) — Represents a compact selectable label for filters, categories, or short choices.
- ChipGroup (core) — Shows a small set of related chips side by side — categories, tags or applied filters — as one labelled group.
- FAB (core) — A single, prominent floating action reachable from anywhere in the current view — optionally expanding into 1-3 closely related actions via a speed-dial.
- Icon (core) — Communicates meaning, action, or status through a recognizable visual symbol.
- IconButton (core) — Triggers an action via a single icon, with no visible text label — a toolbar action, a row action, a close/dismiss control.
- Input (core) — Allows users to enter a single line of free-form text.
- Menu (core) — A Helix-styled, portaled popup listbox anchored to a trigger element — the internal primitive Select uses instead of a native <select> dropdown, and the foundation for any future popup list (Combobox, a context menu, a DatePicker's own internals).
- Modal (core) — A centered overlay that interrupts the page for a focused task or decision — blocks interaction with the rest of the page until dismissed.
- MultiSelect (core) — Lets users choose several values from a predefined list, shown as removable chips inside the field.
- NavItem (core) — A single entry in a persistent navigation list (a SideNav, a tab rail) that links to another view.
- PageHeader (layout) — Introduces a page or major section: title, optional supporting description, and trailing actions in one consistent row.
- RadioButton (core) — A single radio input — the individual option unit RadioGroup renders per choice, exposed on its own for cases that need one radio outside a full group (e.g.
- RadioGroup (core) — Lets users choose exactly one option from a small, visible set of mutually exclusive choices.
- SegmentedControl (core) — Lets users switch between a small, fixed set of mutually exclusive modes or views, with no associated content panel.
- Select (core) — Lets users choose a single value from a predefined list.
- SideNav (layout) — The persistent vertical navigation rail of an app shell — brand mark, primary nav entries, and a footer slot for the current user.
- SidePanel (core) — A modal panel anchored to the right edge of the viewport, for a persistent secondary task alongside — but still blocking — the main page (details, a form, a filter builder).
- Switch (core) — Lets users toggle a single setting on or off, with the change taking effect immediately.
- Table (core) — Displays tabular data edge-to-edge — rows and columns of related records, e.g.
- Textarea (core) — Lets users enter multi-line free-form text.
- Toast (core) — A Sonner-style stacking notification, fixed to the top-right corner, triggered imperatively (toast.success('Saved')) from anywhere — not tied to a piece of UI state the consumer renders conditionally, unlike Modal/SidePanel.
- Tooltip (core) — Reveals a short, non-interactive text label for whatever it wraps, on hover or keyboard focus — identifies an ambiguous control (an icon-only button, an avatar) without adding permanent visible text.
- TopBar (layout) — The fixed-height chrome bar at the top of a page — search, quick actions, and the current user, always in the same place.
<!-- helix:component-list:end -->

## Common mistakes (from real eval runs)

- Toast: render <Toast /> once near the app root, or nothing shows; toast.success(label, description?)
- TopBar slots are start / end (not search/actions, not left/right)
- onPress not onClick · expanded not open · label not title · checked not active · current not active
- Icons by reference: icon={IconPlus}, never icon={<IconPlus />}

## Tokens (semantic layer — use these in app code)

- color.text.*    — neutral, neutral-light, neutral-lightest, disabled, inverse, primary, link, danger, success, warning, info
- color.icon.*    — same roles as text; status icons use icon-*, never text-* (they differ in dark mode)
- color.fill.*    — page, surface, overlay, disabled, {primary|secondary|danger|success|warning|info}-interactive-*, *-light tints
- color.border.*  — neutral(-light|-dark), focus, danger, success, warning, info (+ -light)
- spacing.*       — 3xs 2xs xs s m l xl (2 4 8 12 16 24 32 px)
- radius.*        — none xs s m l xl 2xl 3xl full
- shadow.*        — xs s m l xl focus (only on floating surfaces — ADR-005; Helix is flat)
- textStyle.*     — display / heading / body / caption / label-uppercase / code styles
- size.*          — control heights (ADR-004): s 24 · m 32 · l 40 px
Every color has a light and a dark value; all text/icon pairs are checked for WCAG 2.2 AA in both.

## Architecture decisions (docs/ADR/)

- ADR-001 primitive foundation (native HTML, no primitive kit) · ADR-002 token strategy · ADR-003 AI infrastructure
- ADR-004 size standard · ADR-005 elevation policy · ADR-006/007 motion (Motion library)
- ADR-008/009 Tooltip · ADR-010 Modal & SidePanel · ADR-011 Toast · ADR-012 SegmentedControl · ADR-013 Menu/Select listbox
- ADR-014 icon-agnostic · ADR-015 web components distribution · ADR-016 Accordion timing · ADR-017 icon stroke rule
- ADR-018 stability criteria (how draft/beta/stable is computed)

## Design patterns (.ai/maps/patterns/)

- action-bar — page-level CTAs, toolbars, table batch actions
- disabled-state — any interactive component's disabled state
- empty-state — no data to show (first use, zero results, filtered to nothing)
- expand-collapse-chevron — chevron on anything that opens/closes
- form-field-group — a form with 2-6 fields, submit and inline validation
- form-field-spacing — vertical spacing around a field's label/description/error
- group-spacing — buttons/chips/badges in a group are 4px apart (spacing-2xs)
- motion-effects — whether and how to animate with Motion (incl. drag-to-reorder table rows)
- same-row-sizing — controls on one line share one size
- search-filter — search field + filter buttons over a list or table
- stat-card — labeled metric with a trend delta (dashboard KPI)
- status-row — an item with its current status
- view-toggle — switch between table and cards

## Storybook

- apps/storybook — Storybook 8 (React + Vite); stories in apps/storybook/stories/ (Components/, Layout/, Foundation/, Pages/)
- dev server: pnpm --filter @helix-ds/storybook dev (port 6006) · Status page = live quality table

## AI context

### Terminal queries

When a shell is available, prefer the read-only Helix CLI for focused discovery over loading many
source files: `pnpm helix search "<need>" --json`, `pnpm helix component <Name> --json`,
`pnpm helix token <semantic.path> --json`, or `pnpm helix pattern <name> --json`. Run multiple
lookups as `pnpm helix batch --command "component Button" --command "token color.fill.primary-interactive-default" --json`.
The CLI derives results from the same contracts, tokens, and maps; it is not a second source of truth.

- CLAUDE.md (root + per package) — rules for agents working ON Helix
- AGENTS.md — guide for agents building apps WITH Helix
- .ai/ — maps (prop-map, patterns, figma-map, token exceptions), skills, agents, memory — see .ai/README.md
- evals/prompts — code-generation prompts that check an agent uses Helix correctly (pnpm eval:run / eval:generate)
